evidence_kind: synthetic Java/Python source comparison; not whole-workflow equivalence
notes: Java raw float arrays were serialized x/y/z/class and converted to float32 for this compressed reference fixture.
Iteration 1 memberships are within float32 rounding scale; after one continuing thinning pass 42 of 162180 labels differ.
The iteration 2 membership maximum discrepancy is large despite a low tensor mean; this marks source-state drift and is not accepted as membership equivalence.
Per-label iteration 2 thinning Dice is above 0.9955 and meets the project 0.97 segmentation threshold for this synthetic intermediate only.
No clinical image was used; this is not a full MaCRUISE output comparison.

Iteration-1 registration/growth snapshot: Python registration transform differs from Java by approximately 0.0002 per parameter; post-growth labels differ at 55 voxels and closest-label entries differ at 843 positions. This localizes the first observed discrete split to the registration/growth handoff, without attributing its cause to a specific implementation detail.

Before the second membership update, centroids agree with Java to max absolute error 9.54e-7. Standard deviations differ in five classes on the independently evolved labels; applying the Python variance kernel to the pinned Java labels, memberships, and centroids reproduces the Java standard deviations within 2e-7. This indicates the measured variance split is state-dependent on the prior label divergence, not evidence of a variance-kernel mismatch.

Java source registration on this state starts at energy 0.365961283 and rejects lambda 1.0 and 2/3, accepting 4/9. Python exact-measure gradient and Hessian differ only slightly (max 3.3e-9 and 2.4e-6), but its vectorized energy is 0.365961105 and accepts 2/3. The strict one-step line-search branch therefore diverges. This localizes the remaining numerical sensitivity to registration energy evaluation or prior sampling; the source cannot yet be replicated at this branch boundary.

Using the same Java transform and either Java or Python iteration-1 memberships, Python reproduces the Java registration energy exactly; its transformed shape-prior tensor also matches the Java snapshot bit-for-bit. The 1.93e-8 Python/Java difference in the post-refresh transform alone moves the subsequent registration energy by 1.79e-7 and flips strict line-search acceptance. The split is therefore seeded by the upstream post-refresh transform rounding, not the second-stage energy kernel, on this fixture.
